english.title: Administrative receiver fail to send section 48 report to liquidator
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the administrative receiver of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..) which

(A)_[had gone]_
(B)_[was going]_

into liquidation, without reasonable excuse, failed within 7 days after

(C)_[sending a report in accordance with section 48(1) of the Insolvency Act 1986,]_
(D)_[the nomination of the liquidator,]_
(E)_[the appointment of the liquidator,]_

to send a copy of

(F)_[that report]_
(G)_[the report required under section 48(1) of the Insolvency Act 1986]_

to the liquidator
english.legislation: Contrary to section 48(4) and (8) of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
administrative receiver of company which had gone / was going into liquidation
without reasonable excuse
failed w/i 7 days after sending s48(1) / or the nomination / appointment of the liquidator if later
to send a copy of that report to the liquidator

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.
